title: mkwp blueprint
description: A WordPress site for mkwp to build, with mkwp --blueprint=<file> NAME.

$schema.description: The JSON Schema of the blueprint, for editors. mkwp ignores it.

site.description: The settings of the site. Each is checked like the option with the same name, and an option given on the command line replaces it.

title.description: The title of the site, as with -t/--title.

language.description: The language of the site, as a WordPress locale such as sv_SE, as with -l/--language.

wp.description: The WordPress version, given as <major>, <major>.<minor> or <major>.<minor>.<patch>, as with -W/--wp.

redis.description: Whether to use Redis as object cache, as with -R/--redis.

themes.description: The themes to install. The theme with "activate": true is activated, or, if no theme has it and there is no database, the last one. A theme given with -T/--themes is activated instead.

plugins.description: The plugins to install. Those with "activate": true are activated.

files.description: The files and directories to copy into wp-content, after the themes, plugins and mu-plugins are installed.

source.description: A local file or directory. A relative path is relative to the blueprint's directory, and ~/ is the home directory.

target.description: Where to copy the source, relative to wp-content. As with cp, the target of a file is the path of the copy, such as uploads/2024/01/logo.png, so the copy can get a new name, and a target that ends with /, or is a directory that already exists, is the directory to copy the file into under its own name. The target of a directory is the directory to merge its contents into, such as uploads. Missing directories are created. The target must not be absolute or start with ~, and its .. parts must not lead out of wp-content.

database.description: A database to start the site from: a dump or a DDEV snapshot of another WordPress site, whose tables have the prefix wp_. It has exactly one of dump and snapshot. The site keeps the users, settings and active theme and plugins of the database, but its old address is replaced by the site's, the database is upgraded, mkwp's user is made an administrator, a title and language given explicitly replace those of the database, and themes and plugins with "activate": true are activated. A dump or a snapshot can hold secrets, such as licence keys and API credentials, which mkwp doesn't remove.

dump.description: The dump: plain SQL in a .sql file, or gzip-compressed SQL in a .sql.gz file. A relative path is relative to the blueprint's directory, and ~/ is the home directory.

snapshot.description: The snapshot: a file made by ddev snapshot, such as one in a site's .ddev/db_snapshots, with the name DDEV gave it, which ends with the server it was taken from, as in site-mariadb_11.8.zst. It can be anywhere. A relative path is relative to the blueprint's directory, and ~/ is the home directory. It needs server.

server.description: The database server to import the dump into, or to restore the snapshot into, as mariadb:<version> or mysql:<version>, e.g. mariadb:11.8, with a version that DDEV has. With a snapshot, it's required, and must be the server the snapshot was taken from. With a dump, DDEV's default server is used if it's omitted.

wp_cli.description: WP-CLI commands to run, in the given order, at the end of the build: after Redis is enabled and before the site is opened. If a command fails, mkwp stops without opening the site.

items.description: A WP-CLI command: the arguments to wp, without wp itself, such as ["option", "update", "blogdescription", "Just another site"]. Each argument reaches WP-CLI exactly as written, with no shell in between, so nothing needs quoting. The command gets no input, so give --yes to a command that asks for confirmation.

note.description: A note of your own, since JSON has no comments. mkwp ignores it.

item.description: A theme or plugin: its source, or an object with its source.

version.description: The version to install, such as 1.6. Only a slug on WordPress.org can have it.

ref.description: The tag, branch or commit to check out instead of the latest tag. Only a Git repository can have it.

activate.description: Whether to activate the theme or plugin. At most one theme may have it.

source.description: Where a theme or plugin comes from, recognized in this order: a local directory or zip file, if it starts with ./, ../, / or ~/, where a relative path is relative to the blueprint's directory; a Git repository, if it ends with .git, where the latest tag or the ref is checked out; a zip file at a URL, if it starts with http:// or https://; and otherwise a slug on WordPress.org.

git.description: A Git repository: a URL that ends with .git and is not a local path.

marked.description: A theme or plugin with "activate": true.

mu_plugin.description: An mu-plugin: its source, or an object with its source.

mu_plugin_source.description: Where an mu-plugin comes from: a local PHP file, if it starts with ./, ../, / or ~/, where a relative path is relative to the blueprint's directory, or the URL of a PHP file.
